top_story.headline: No Labels PAC reports $7.79 million in member contributions steered to candidates of both parties
top_story.dek: A Form 99 filed October 20 says members gave through the Democracy Engine platform after solicitations made under the group's internal communication allowance.
paragraphs: No Labels PAC told the FEC that during the current reporting period it used its "internal communication" allowance to solicit No Labels members to contribute directly to aligned candidates through the Democracy Engine platform. The filing says members gave a total of $7,786,591.11 in the period. It lists the amount going to each of roughly 35 candidates and committees, including $47,775 to Rep. Jared Moskowitz, $20,675 to Rep. Thomas Suozzi and $19,750 to Rep. Hillary Scholten.

The filing also gives cycle-to-date totals for the 2026 election cycle. The largest are $726,028.81 for Sen. Susan Collins, $710,845.38 for Sen. Bill Cassidy, $409,602.90 for Rep. Josh Gottheimer and $358,051.72 for Rep. Mike Lawler. The list also includes the Lawler Victory Fund and LA Victory ($297,000).

The five-page filing is a plain list of figures and does not say how the funds were routed or whether any compliance question prompted it. The amounts are the committee's own statement, not an FEC finding.

The other notable item from today is a May-to-October-cycle compliance request to Club for Growth PAC, whose amended August Monthly report drew questions about apparent corporate contributions, $19,000 in earmarked contributions with no matching receipts, and independent expenditures supporting Derek Merrin and Scott Perry that appear to have been disseminated after their primaries. Its response is due 11/24.

sections.headline: One sitting member's committee corrects its 48-hour report
paragraphs: One filing today is tagged to a sitting lawmaker. It is a routine correction.

items: Rep. Keith Self (R-TX) amends a 48-hour report to add two earmarked individual donations. His committee, Self for Congress, says it was notified of the earmarks after the report date, and that the PAC donation was previously reported. The amendment covers 10/15/26 to 10/17/26. (Form 99)

sections.headline: Ten new RFAIs, led by Club for Growth PAC's three-part inquiry
paragraphs: Ten RFAIs went out on October 20, each with a response due date of 11/24/2026. Four are to candidate committees and six to PACs and party committees. Most are template items: Column B total errors, unclear disbursement purposes, earmarked contributions and excessive contributions. The Club for Growth PAC letter is the most substantive. No treasurer is shared among these ten.

items: FEC asks Club for Growth PAC about apparent corporate or LLC contributions, $19,000 in earmarked contributions with no Schedule A entries, and independent expenditures for Derek Merrin and Scott Perry that appear to have been disseminated after their primaries. The letter concerns the amended August Monthly report received 09/20/2026. Treasurer is Adam Rozansky. (RFAI)

FEC says Republican Voters of Texas PAC may have failed to file timely 24-hour reports on last-minute independent expenditures. It also asks why the amended April Quarterly report shows receipts down $69,710.97 and disbursements down $45,500.44 from the original. Treasurer is Linda Stuckey. (RFAI)

FEC asks Kern County Republican Central Committee (FED) to explain a Schedule H2 ratio for an "IE" activity that it reported as unchanged though the event was not previously reported. Treasurer is Tim Collins. (RFAI)

FEC asks Nevada County Republican Party whether receipts labeled "Miscellaneous Small Donations" include any individual's contributions above $200 for the year. If so, they must be itemized. Treasurer is Tammie Siller. (RFAI)
FEC says the Column B totals on the July Quarterly report of Do Not Use Teresa Leger Fernandez Victory Fund appear incorrect on a dozen lines. Treasurer is Steven Fitzer. (RFAI)

FEC says Column B totals and line categories are wrong on the July Quarterly report of Seventh Congressional District Republican Party of Minnesota. Contributions to federal candidates and committees belong on a separate Schedule B supporting Line 23. Treasurer is Gregg Allan Kulberg. (RFAI)

FEC asks Darden Copeland for Congress why 48-hour-notice contributions are missing from Schedule A of its amended Year-End 2025 report. It also flags a disbursement described only as "Consulting" and ActBlue earmark reporting. The candidate is Darden Hunter Copeland (D-TN), a challenger. Treasurer is Jefferson Cole Dowsley Jr. (RFAI)

FEC asks Friends of Joy Hoover to correct Column B totals and explain a $13,500 drop in both receipts and disbursements. The drop is on its amended April Quarterly report compared with the original. The candidate, Joy Hoover (D-NV), is also listed as treasurer. (RFAI)

FEC asks Gregg Mele for America whether an $8,290 "Loan for Candidate Paid Expenses Itemized" was really a candidate advance or reimbursement. The candidate is Gregg Mele (R-NJ, open seat). Treasurer is Jason D. Boles. (RFAI)

FEC says Scott Singer for Congress holds excessive contributions not refunded, redesignated or reattributed within 60 days. It also says the October Quarterly report does not clearly tie conduit memo entries to earmarked contributions. The letter notes the committee's own explanation of some corrective action. The candidate is Scott M. Singer (R-FL), a challenger. Treasurer is Bradley T. Crate. (RFAI)

sections.headline: Threshold statements, loan forgiveness letters, RFAI responses and two cross-filed Emmett White reports
paragraphs: Twenty-one non-termination Form 99s came in. Most are mundane: committees below the $5,000 reporting threshold, candidates forgiving loans and committees answering RFAIs. Three stand out. No Labels PAC is the Top Story. Altria Group, Inc. Political Action Committee hit red-flag keywords, but they come from the bank's attached boilerplate. The two Emmett White filings appear to have been submitted under each other's committee IDs.
Emmett Lee White signed both of the cross-filed reports as treasurer.

items: Altria Group, Inc. Political Action Committee tells the FEC it took a $100,000 loan from Chain Bridge Bank, N.A.. The Schedule C shows an 8.00% rate, incurred 08/06/2026 and due 08/06/2027. The Schedule C-1 was signed October 7 by treasurer John Mason and bank president David Evinger. The cover letter is dated October 15 and the filing was received October 20. The C-1 appears to pledge future contributions or receipts as collateral, but the text is garbled. The keyword hits for fraud, money laundering and theft come from the bank's attached legal and e-sign text, not from the committee's own statements. (Form 99)
DCCC files a 29-page C-1/Loan Agreement. The text layer shows only the cover page, so the loan terms could not be read. (Form 99)

Emmett White (C00880609) files what appears to be Emmett Lee White for President's 12-Day Pre-General Form 3P. The report body names presidential committee C00931535, which is not the committee ID it was filed under. It covers 07/31 to 10/18 on the summary page but shows 09/15 on later pages. Summary receipts and disbursements for the period are zero, while cycle-to-date receipts are $52,115.61 and debts owed by the committee are $7,260.55. (Form 99)

Emmett Lee White's presidential committee files what appears to be a Form 3X for "Hope Community Shelter," C00880609, covering 08/15 to 09/30. It reports one $25 itemized receipt from Jaime Peters dated 09/23/2026. It was received 10/19, two days before this edition. The Form 3X and the Form 3P above appear to have been filed under each other's committee IDs. (Form 99)

Committee to Elect Lamont Lavender for Senate tells the FEC its 2026 campaign activity is suspended with no receipts or spending. The statement says he is "late filing due to computer issues," a late disclosure by his own account. He says he may run in 2028 (Lamont Lavender, D-AL, open seat). It was received 10/19. (Form 99)

Nila for Congress tells the FEC it refunded $4,100 in excessive contributions on October 20, after the 60-day deadline. The refunds were $3,500 to Gary McCollum, $500 to Arthur Roberson and $100 to Kiran S. Debnath, with $1,000 of McCollum's reattributed to his spouse, Fredericka McCollum. The committee blames a former compliance vendor and says the work is now in-house. It responds to a September 15 RFAI. Treasurer is Daniel Jimenez (Nila Devanath, D-VA). (Form 99)

Lucero for Congress Inc. says contributions accepted for the General 2026 and not refunded were redesignated to the Primary 2028. It says it holds written letters from each contributor and that a "miss communication" led it to think the funds could pay debt. The candidate is Rob Lucero (D-CA), a challenger. (Form 99)

Knife River Corporation PAC tells the FEC it does not qualify for multicandidate status. The separate segregated fund says it has about 30 unique employee contributors, short of the 51 required. It responds to an RFAI. (Form 99)

Sam Husseini for Congress files a second amended October 15 report. The amendment adds a missing $100 donation from Duane Roth dated 8/14/2026. It also corrects donor data for Connie Wen, merges the Soody Tronson and Soodabeh Tronson records, and updates the occupation and employer of Robin Eastman-Abaya. (Form 99)

The Wisco Project PAC lowers its reported ad buy supporting Rebecca Cooke in Wisconsin's 3rd District. The amended 48-hour notice cuts the Budget Signs & Specialties expenditure from $1,378.19 to $1,217.63. The original used a vendor estimate. (Form 99)
Heidi Hall for Congress says candidate Heidi Hall (D-CA) forgave $76,374.88 in interest-free personal loans to her committee. The letter is dated September 30 and was received October 20. (Form 99)

Mel Tull for Congress says candidate Melvin E. Tull III (D-VA) forgave $74,252.73 in remaining loans. The letter ties the forgiveness to the committee's termination filing covering July 16 through August 31. It is dated October 12. (Form 99)
Indigo PAC reports that John McCrea forgave $855.23 in debts and loans owed to him on 09/30/2026. (Form 99)

Rights Of Americans Association asks the FEC to approve its termination. Treasurer Tamika La'Shon Hill says debts are paid, cash on hand is $0.00 and the bank account is closed. The committee acknowledges it must keep filing reports until the FEC approves. (Form 99)

Hope For Tomorrow - Alan Bond For Congress says it has not passed the $5,000 threshold for detailed reporting. The statement reports donations of $3,795.71, expenses of $3,131.10 and $1,045.54 cash on hand at the October 14 close of books. Alan Bond (I-NJ) is a challenger. (Form 99)
Committee to Elect Mike Saliba says it has not met the $5,000 reporting threshold. Mike Saliba (L-MI) is running in an open seat. (Form 99)
Cooke C Harvey for Congress says it has not met the $5,000 reporting threshold. Cooke Costa Harvey (I-VA) is a challenger. (Form 99)

JJJOHNSON2028 tells the FEC that 21 banks have refused to open a campaign account and that he cannot follow FEC rules. The statement from JJ Johnson (D, 2028 presidential) says he does not care about fines. It also accuses the FEC of being "compromised" and cites a lawsuit he filed on PACER. (Form 99)

JJJOHNSON2028 files a second statement the same day repeating the 21 bank refusals. It again accuses the FEC of silence and election interference, and repeats the claim that his lawsuit is on PACER. (Form 99)

The Campaign Committee to Elect Clifford G. Fleetwood for U.S. Congress submits a motion to halt Florida's 20th District general election. The filing is styled as a federal racketeering complaint against Ron DeSantis, Debbie Wasserman Schultz and others, alleging illegal removal from the ballot. The case number is blank and the filing addresses Judge James E. Boasberg. It is not a campaign-finance filing and its claims are the filer's allegations. The candidate is Clifford Gene Fleetwood (Unaffiliated, FL). (Form 99)
